newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Stock records tumble in European bull run.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Stock records tumble in European bull run.

text.p: European stock markets headed into record territory again on Wednesday buoyed by Wall Street gains and a strong dollar, with new highs in London and Frankfurt encouraging investors on smaller bourses to join the party.

In currencies, the dollar traded comfortably above 1.79 marks and 115 yen as the market awaited a German Cabinet statement after 1230 GMT which was expected to reaffirm its policy of a strong deutschemark and single European currency.

Germany's 30-share DAX index was up about 80 points and touched a record 4,202.05 in late trading. Dealers saw the DAX establishing itself above 4,200 points this week, underpinned by the firmer dollar and Wall Street gains.
Retailer Karstadt was among top percentage gainers, rising five percent to 657 marks despite market speculation that the shop group may be dropped from the DAX in favour of Adidas.
"The buy orders are coming into the market without end," said one Frankfurt dealer. "It's the same thing every day. There are no sell orders, only buyers from a broad spectrum."
The FTSE 100, Britain's leading share index, stayed sharply higher by late morning on Wednesday, hovering near its all-time best on a renewed surge in bank stocks.
At 1100 GMT, the FTSE 100 traded 57.6 points higher at 4,956.9 as traders looked at the next 100-point hurdle at 5,000.

"There is certainly talk about 5,000," one market maker said. "I doubt we will see it today but there is still bid talk going on, there is cash around and with any more corporate news, then it will be off to the races. This is a major squeeze."
Buying spread to other heavyweight stocks in the brewing and pharmaceutical sectors and the broader FTSE 250 index.
French shares settled below a fresh all-time high of 2,995.38 while the July future hit 3,000 points.
One trader said a domestic bond maturity explained part of the rise, adding: "All markets are at record highs and Paris follows."
Swiss shares posted early gains of around one percent, profiting particularly from higher prices for pharmaceutical companies and major banks.
Dutch shares zoomed to a new record at the opening, and dealers said the market could not go wrong today.

The Dow climbed 53 points on Tuesday to hit the blue chip average's first new high in a week. U.S. stocks trading in London on Wednesday indicated a higher opening on Wall Street but this would depend on U.S. June consumer price data, due at 1230 GMT.
The dollar traded steadily above 1.79 marks in morning Europe, the mark was itself steady against other European currencies with attention on the German Cabinet regular news conference.
"Tomorrow we will say that we are for a strong euro and for a strong mark," German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday.
The dollar was firm around 115.80 yen, and the Bank of Japan said monetary policy was still aimed at fostering economic growth.
Separately, dealers in Stockholm said the Swedish Riksbank, the central bank, sold crowns for dollars on Wednesday at 7.8550.

The British pound pushed higher against the mark on expectations of an interest rate rise, fanned by the published minutes of the June UK monetary policy committee meeting showing unanimity on interest rate policy.
Sterling traded at 3.0145 marks from 3.0178 late on Tuesday. CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was at 115.87 yen and 1.7928 marks compared with 115.74 yen and 1.8013 marks in late trading on Tuesday. STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 57.6 points at 4,956.9.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 68.93 points at 4,190.06.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 25.75 points at 2,976.45.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London at $319.50, 75 cents off the Tuesday afternoon fix.
Silver was at $4.32, against a previous $4.33 London close.
